name: Ishita Dasgupta
bio: My graduate research is focused on leveraging microfluidics to establish a host-bacterial coculture model of colorectal cancer.

name: Jaime Greatorex
bio: My graduate research utilizes microfluidics to investigate how gut microbes shape the development of intestinal organoids and epithelium, and to establish the optimum conditions for determining the spatiotemporal dynamics within a group of bacterial species.

name: Liya Patel
bio: My research focuses on studying liver function in microfluidic devices.

name: Diana Brizzolara
bio: My goal is to design and test microfluidic devices that allow for spatial control of oxygen, capable of generating localized gradients.

name: Maria Cohen
bio: My graduate research investigates bacterial chemotaxis through the development of a microfluidic platform designed to measure and compare migration.

name: Kyla Narayan
bio: My project uses a physics-informed neural network to model 2D oxygen diffusion in a tissue scaffold.

name: Julia Gerber
bio: My project involves building and testing microfluidic devices for bacterial chemotaxis.

name: Katerina Muchacho
bio: My project explores how different growth environments and spatial orientations affect bacterial growth, with a focus on how these conditions influence bacterial quorum sensing and communication.

name: Tengis Munkhbat
bio: My current goal is to build an algorithm to predict hepatotoxicity.

name: Dominique Orbea
bio: My project focuses on the genetic modification of bacteria via transformation with a fluorescent reporter plasmid and the study of bacterial surface attachment under different conditions.
